lead.headline: Wall Street Caps Its Best Week Since April 2025 With a Black Friday Rally, as Seoul and Shanghai Surge and a December Fed Hike Becomes a Near-Certainty
lead.dek: The S&P 500 rose 1.6% to 7,297 in Friday's half-day and about 5.6% from last week's low, while the 10-year yield climbed to 4.94%, gold jumped about 3% and Brent's expiring contract held near $95 ahead of Sunday's OPEC+ meeting.
body: Global stocks ended a turbulent week with a broad rally. In New York's shortened Black Friday session on 27 Nov, the S&P 500 gained 1.60% to 7,297.49, the Nasdaq Composite 2.31% to 24,129.50 and the Dow 591.99 points to 50,774.94. Measured from the 20 Nov low, the S&P 500 rose about 5.6% on the week, its best week since April 2025 according to Capp Notes, with all 11 sectors higher on Friday and chipmakers leading as the semiconductor index climbed 4.69%.

Asia set the tone earlier in the day. Seoul's Kospi jumped 4.34% to 4,915.68 a day after the Bank of Korea's hike, the Shanghai Composite rose 3.73% after a State Council pledge to support the market, and the Nikkei 225 and Hang Seng each gained 2.11%. Europe's STOXX 600 added 1.08% to a one-week high of 643.85. India was the exception: the Sensex fell 989 points to 83,339.26 as IT stocks slid, even as foreign investors bought for a 19th straight session.

The rally came in spite of, not because of, rates. The 10-year Treasury yield rose 9bp to 4.94% and CME FedWatch put the odds of a 25bp hike at the 8-9 Dec meeting at 97.4%, after hotter core PCE data and an upgrade of third-quarter GDP growth to 4.3%. The dollar index firmed to 104.04 and the yen weakened to 159.55.

The war in the Gulf still sets the floor under commodities. Brent's expiring January contract settled at $95.44, down 1.2% on the day but about 3% higher on the week, as the IRGC claimed new tanker mine strikes near Khasab and Tehran confirmed Qatari and Pakistani mediation with Washington. Gold rose to about $3,668 and silver 9%. OPEC+ meets on Sunday on 2027 quotas, Spain votes the same day, and S&P's after-hours move to a negative outlook on France greets European bond markets on Monday.

impact.title: What it means for markets
points: The rebound ran on thin holiday volume, so Monday's full sessions and Tuesday's ISM and JOLTS data are the first real test; the VIX is down to about 23.8 from 35.89 on 20 Nov but remains well above October's 19.42.

With a December Fed hike about 97% priced and the 10-year near 4.94%, equities are rallying against tighter money; long-duration tech and bitcoin, which slipped below $60,000, remain the most rate-sensitive pockets.

Oil's war premium is concentrated in the prompt month: the expiring January Brent contract settled roughly $4-5 above the next contract, pointing to an acute rather than lasting squeeze ahead of OPEC+ on 29 Nov.
Europe faces two event risks at Monday's open: S&P's negative outlook on France for OAT spreads and Spain's Sunday election for Bonos and Spanish banks.

read.title: The Ledger's Read
paragraphs: This was the week markets stopped panicking without stopping worrying. From the 20 Nov low, the S&P 500 recovered about 5.6% and the VIX fell from almost 36 to under 24, a move led by the same chip and memory stocks that had led the sell-off. Seoul, Tokyo, Shanghai and Europe joined in. But the rally happened on thin holiday volume and with November still a losing month, so it is better read as a repair of positioning, after hedge funds piled into ETF shorts, than as a new uptrend.

The striking feature is that stocks rose while the policy backdrop tightened. Markets now price a December Fed hike at about 97%, the 10-year yield is back at 4.94%, the Bank of Korea has already moved, and Tokyo inflation keeps the BoJ in play. That combination tends to favour banks and cyclicals over long-duration growth, and it explains why bitcoin, a pure duration-and-liquidity asset, fell even as the Nasdaq jumped. India's slide on a day of global gains shows how quickly crowded trades can unwind when foreign investors hedge with futures while buying cash.

The next week is crowded with event risk. OPEC+ meets on Sunday as Brent's prompt contract trades several dollars above the next month and Gulf attacks continue; Spain votes the same day; France's bond market opens Monday under a negative S&P outlook; India and Canada report GDP on Monday; and ISM, JOLTS and the jobs report will decide whether the Fed's December move is the last in this cycle or one of several. A Gulf de-escalation through the Qatari and Pakistani channels would be the biggest upside surprise for risk; a successful mass strike on energy infrastructure, in the Gulf or in Ukraine, the biggest downside one.

body: US stocks extended their recovery in the shortened post-Thanksgiving session on 27 Nov. The S&P 500 finished at 7,297.49 (+1.60%), the Nasdaq Composite at 24,129.50 (+2.31%), the Nasdaq-100 at 26,726.39 (+2.61%), the Dow at 50,774.94 (+1.18%) and the Russell 2000 at 2,750.30 (+1.71%), according to Yahoo Finance and other closing reports. The week marked a sharp turn from the 20 Nov lows, when the S&P 500 closed at 6,910.39 and the VIX at 35.89. Using that base, the S&P 500 gained about 5.6% and the Dow about 5.5%; Capp Notes calls it the S&P 500's best week since April 2025. Gains were broad. Capp Notes counts 406 S&P 500 advancers against 94 decliners and gains in all 11 sectors, led by technology (+2.80%), as the semiconductor index climbed 4.69%. Brazil-linked shares surged after Lula named Bradesco chairman Luiz Carlos Trabuco as finance minister, and Amazon rose 3.96% as Black Friday online sales ran ahead of forecasts.

The month as a whole is still negative: the S&P 500 sits about 3.7% below its 31 Oct close of 7,580.07 and 6.7% below its 6 Oct record close of 7,818.93, per The Company Chronicle. Rates remain the main headwind, with the 10-year Treasury yield up 9bp to 4.94% on Friday and CME FedWatch putting the odds of a 25bp December hike at 97.4%.

stories.headline: Iran War, Day 274: IRGC Claims Two More Tanker Blasts Off Khasab as Tehran Confirms Qatari and Pakistani Mediation, and Brent Books Its First Weekly Gain of November
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards navy said on 27 Nov, via IRNA, that one tanker struck a mine at the entrance to Oman's Khasab port and a second exploded and burned east of the Strait of Hormuz on what it called an unauthorised route; no ships were named and the claims are unverified. Kuwait summoned Iran's ambassador the same day over what it called continuing attacks, after blaming Iranian drones for two deaths on 26 Nov. Foreign Minister Araghchi confirmed that Qatar and Pakistan are mediating with Washington and that their proposals are under review, while insisting the strait stays shut until Iran's demands are met. President Trump told troops on Thanksgiving that victory is 'at hand' and that the US would hit the Pickaxe Mountain site if Iran acts. Brent settled $1.13 (1.2%) lower at $95.44 on 27 Nov, still up about 3% on the week.
stories.market: Brent's $95.44 settle (27 Nov) left it about 3% higher on the week, its first weekly gain in November, as tanker and Saudi refinery attacks offset relief that Washington has not escalated; war-risk cover in Hormuz is quoted at 6-9% of hull value (26 Nov), and Qatar has extended LNG force majeure on some cargoes to end-December, a link into European gas.

body: The IRGC navy's latest statement, posted by IRNA on 27 Nov, described two more tanker incidents: one vessel struck a mine at the mouth of Khasab port on Oman's Musandam peninsula, and a second exploded and caught fire after sailing east of the strait. As in earlier claims, the Guards said both ships had switched off their tracking systems to slip through what Tehran calls a 'fake' route under US protection. No vessel names, owners or casualty details have been released, and no independent confirmation from UKMTO or shipowners appeared in reports by Saturday morning. Iran's regular navy repeated that the strait will not reopen until Tehran's goals are met.

Kuwait summoned the Iranian ambassador on 27 Nov over what it called continuing attacks, a day after it said debris from intercepted Iranian drones killed two Italian technicians; Iran's military has denied operating in the area. Iranian army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia said ships that do not coordinate with Iran's forces have faced serious risks in recent weeks.

On diplomacy, Araghchi acknowledged on 26 Nov that Tehran is talking to Washington through Qatari and Pakistani mediators and that their proposals are being reviewed, and Qatar's Majed al-Ansari said both sides were engaged in mediation. That sits awkwardly with parliament speaker Ghalibaf's line that no talks can happen before seven conditions are met, including an end to the US blockade, sanctions relief, release of frozen assets and reparations; Secretary of State Rubio has called that list outrageous.

Trump, speaking to deployed troops from Mar-a-Lago on Thanksgiving, said victory was at hand and would come when he decided, called the operation the largest naval blockade in history, and said the US would 'absolutely' strike the Pickaxe Mountain site if Iran took action, while adding that he would prefer a deal. He said US forces had fired 150 missiles to intercept threats to shipping in the strait.

In markets, Brent settled at $95.44 on 27 Nov, down $1.13 on the day, and WTI at $83.08, down 60 cents from Wednesday. Brent still rose about 3% on the week after three weekly losses. Traders weighed the tanker and Saudi refinery attacks against relief that the US had not escalated, and OPEC+ is expected on Sunday to keep first-quarter 2027 targets unchanged, according to sources cited in the same report. Qatar has extended force majeure on some LNG cargoes to at least the end of December, Trading Economics reported.

stories.headline: Saudi Arabia's Pact Allies Condemn the Houthi Attacks but Announce No New Steps, as Houthi Media Say a Saudi Strike Killed 11 in Taiz
stories.summary: Senior officials from Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye, meeting in Islamabad on 27 Nov as the committee of their Mecca defence pact, condemned what they called persistent Houthi attacks on Saudi civilians and infrastructure and pledged to step up support, but announced no concrete measures; Pakistan has ruled out attacking inside Yemen. Saudi authorities say at least 26 people have been killed in suspected Houthi drone and missile attacks in the kingdom since 23 Sep, 23 of them at airports. Houthi-run media said a Saudi air strike on al-Turbah, south of Taiz city, killed 11 civilians on 27 Nov, a claim Al Jazeera could not verify. The coalition said it destroyed a Houthi drone launched toward the Riyadh region the same day, a day after a projectile hit Aramco's Jazan refinery.
stories.market: The Saudi Red Sea outlet is now priced as a war zone: war-risk quotes for Saudi-linked tankers run about 3% of hull value at Yanbu and about 7% further south (as of 26 Nov), carriers are adding surcharges at Jeddah, and Riyadh's state pool has cut cargo cover costs 50-60%; Brent's 27 Nov settle of $95.44 still carries the refinery risk.

body: The Mecca pact's Strategic Political and Defence Committee met for about two and a half hours in Islamabad on 27 Nov. Pakistan's foreign minister Ishaq Dar read a joint statement condemning the Houthi strikes and promising to intensify support for Saudi security under the treaty's collective-defence clause. No new deployments were announced: Türkiye's Hakan Fidan said no decision had been taken on troops inside Yemen, and Pakistan has pledged to defend Saudi territory but not to attack the Houthis in Yemen. Türkiye has completed ratification of the pact.

The meeting followed a week in which the Houthis targeted Saudi energy and financial sites almost daily, including Aramco's 400,000 b/d Jazan refinery on 26 Nov and Ras Tanura a day earlier. Saudi authorities count at least 26 deaths in the kingdom from suspected Houthi attacks since 23 Sep. On 27 Nov the coalition said it shot down a drone launched toward the Riyadh region.

Houthi media said a Saudi strike on a residential building in al-Turbah in Taiz governorate killed 11 people on 27 Nov; rescuers recovered eight bodies and three people were missing, and the coalition did not immediately comment. The WHO puts casualties in Yemen at about 13,343 killed or injured since August, and the Houthis still hold 73 UN staff.

For shipping, the threat to Saudi Red Sea ports is already in prices. Enterprise reported that no major carrier has dropped Jeddah, which handled a record 582,900 TEU in October, but lines are adding surcharges even on existing contracts and offering free rerouting to King Abdullah Port. War-risk quotes for Saudi-linked tankers are about 3% of hull value at Yanbu and about 7% for calls further south, versus 6-9% in Hormuz. About 70% of Yanbu's crude now sails north, and Asia-bound cargoes take about eight weeks instead of four.

stories.summary: Izzeldeen al-Hayya, son of Hamas's Gaza chief Khalil al-Hayya, survived a dawn Israeli air strike on 27 Nov with his family, Hamas said, while Israeli attacks killed four Palestinians elsewhere in Gaza. Gaza's health ministry says at least 1,705 people have been killed and 6,163 wounded since the October 2025 ceasefire and 74,772 since October 2023. The IDF said its strikes last week killed four Hamas operatives it accused of violating the truce. In Lebanon, Israeli jets and artillery hit al-Qantara, Kfar Tebnit and the coast south of Tyre on 27 Nov, and drones flew low over Beirut's southern suburbs. In Israel, Eisenkot has nine days left to form a government.
stories.market: The market link is indirect: Israeli coalition talks and the defence budget drive the shekel and Israeli bonds, Lebanon's defaulted Eurobonds hinge on the June ceasefire holding, and Israel's push for renewed Iran strikes ties the front to oil.

body: Hamas official Basem Naim said Izzeldeen al-Hayya, 29, and his family survived an Israeli strike at dawn on 27 Nov, with several relatives wounded; Hamas called it an assassination attempt and linked it to threats by Defence Minister Katz. Four of the Hamas leader's sons have been killed in earlier Israeli strikes. Separately, a drone strike on a vehicle west of Jabalia killed one man and civil defence teams recovered three bodies in Rafah.

The IDF said strikes in the past week killed four Hamas members, including a deputy cell commander it linked to the 7 October attack, saying they were acting in systematic violation of the ceasefire. Gaza's health ministry now counts 1,705 deaths and 6,163 injuries since the October 2025 truce. UN agencies say 67% of Gaza's population still faces crisis-level hunger or worse. Israel's security cabinet was reported to be meeting on advancing Trump's Gaza plan under US pressure.

In Lebanon, the state news agency reported Israeli air strikes on al-Qantara, Kfar Tebnit and areas near Zawtar al-Sharqiya on 27 Nov, plus heavy shelling on the al-Mansouri coast, a day after the air force hit dozens of rockets and launchers at a Radwan Force camp. No casualties were reported. Lebanese authorities say more than 4,300 people have been killed and over a million displaced since the 2 March escalation; the 26 June US-mediated deal provides for a gradual Israeli withdrawal and Hezbollah's disarmament.

In Israeli politics, Eisenkot has nine days left on his mandate unless President Herzog extends it. He has signed deals with the Democrats and Yisrael Beytenu and is talking to United Torah Judaism, while Ra'am's leader was expected to say on Saturday that he recognises Hamas as a terror group, a condition Eisenkot has set for every partner.

stories.summary: Russia launched 155 strike drones overnight to 27 Nov, 110 of which were shot down, hitting energy, rail and civilian sites in nine regions and cutting power to some consumers in six, Prime Minister Koretsky said; at least four people were killed. Ukraine's General Staff said it struck the Efremov synthetic-rubber plant in Tula region, which it says supplies solid fuel components for Iskander missiles, along with a Rosatom heat-and-power plant, and that the earlier strike on the 7.5 million-tonne Novoshakhtinsk refinery destroyed 20 storage tanks. Russia said it downed 318 drones, including 45 over St Petersburg and the Leningrad region. The larger Russian energy strike that Zelensky warned of on 26 Nov had not been reported by Saturday morning, and US envoy Kushner described peace talks as in a partial deadlock over territory.

body: Russia's overnight attack to 27 Nov used 155 strike drones, 51 of them jet-powered, plus decoys; Ukraine said it downed 110. Koretsky said railway, energy, industrial and residential sites were hit in nine regions, and some consumers lost power in Dnipropetrovsk, Zaporizhzhia, Kirovohrad, Sumy, Kharkiv and Kherson. Deaths were reported in Nizhyn, Izium and Kryvyi Rih. Since September Russia has made more than 1,000 strikes on Ukraine's energy system, and Kyiv halted all electricity exports after the 20 Nov attack, with imports at their highest since mid-June.

Ukraine kept up its own campaign. The General Staff said it hit the Efremov synthetic-rubber plant in Tula region, at least the third strike on the site in a year, and Euronews reported a Rosatom-owned combined heat and power plant there was also hit. It confirmed the earlier strike on the Novoshakhtinsk refinery in Rostov region, capacity up to 7.5 million tonnes a year, destroyed 20 horizontal tanks and damaged 32 more. Russia said it downed 318 drones over 10 regions and Crimea, including 45 around St Petersburg.

Zelensky warned on 26 Nov that Moscow is completing preparations for a new massive strike on energy, logistics and critical services, and asked for more Patriot interceptors, in short supply since the Iran war. Kushner, mediating with Witkoff, said Putin had agreed not to use nuclear weapons but that talks were in a partial deadlock over Ukrainian territory.

Gas markets looked through the headlines. TTF front-month closed at €84.47/MWh on 27 Nov, down 3.57% from €87.60, on a possible recovery in Norwegian flows and signs that well-stocked Chinese utilities could free LNG for Europe, Trading Economics reported; it was down more than 3% on the week. Below-normal temperatures in Germany and eastern Europe and Qatar's extended LNG force majeure are the upside risks, with storage under 68% full.

stories.headline: Sudan's Army Says It Has Retaken the Gold-Mining Town of Maqanza Near Ed Damazin as More Than 15,000 Troops Reach the Blue Nile Capital
stories.summary: Sudanese military sources said on 27 Nov that the army had recaptured Maqanza, an artisanal gold-mining town in Bau locality about 22 km from Ed Damazin that the RSF and its SPLM-N allies entered on 21 Nov; the army has issued no official confirmation. The same sources said more than 15,000 army personnel had arrived in Ed Damazin, after drone strikes on the city and on the Roseires dam area killed at least 17 earlier in the week. The Emergency Lawyers group estimates 1,620-1,890 people fled Maqanza, and a civil-society initiative counts over 51,000 newly displaced in Blue Nile as of 22 Nov. Sudan has also rejected Ethiopia's offer to host peace talks and is reinforcing Gedaref state on the Ethiopian border.
stories.market: Sudan's channels are gold output and smuggling, Port Sudan's Red Sea trade and power from the Roseires dam; spot gold closed $3,653.53 on 27 Nov, up 2.43% on the day and 3.25% on the week, a move driven by rates and the dollar rather than the war.

body: Maqanza, in Bau locality, was the RSF-SPLM-N alliance's most advanced gain toward Ed Damazin; the RSF announced its capture after entering on 21 Nov. Military sources told Asharq Al-Awsat on 27 Nov that the army had taken it back, though no official statement followed. The town is known for artisanal gold mining and was once the headquarters of Malik Agar's SPLM.

The same sources said more than 15,000 troops had arrived in Ed Damazin, the Blue Nile capital, following the arrival of Sudan Shield Forces reinforcements reported on 26 Nov. Drone strikes on Ed Damazin and Roseires on 24 Nov killed at least 14 according to a hospital source, and 19 according to Emergency Lawyers, and hit power infrastructure at the Roseires dam. A Sudanese military source said the drones were launched from Ethiopia, which Addis Ababa denies.

Displacement is rising: IOM counted nearly 120,000 displaced in Blue Nile between January and mid-October, and civil-society monitors more than 51,000 newly displaced as of 22 Nov. In West Kordofan, IOM said at least 795 people fled Abu Zabad on 25 Nov, and a drone strike on a passenger truck near Ghubeish killed at least 11 on 26 Nov.

On diplomacy, Khartoum rejected Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's offer to host talks and urged the African Union to exclude Ethiopia from mediation, and announced reinforcements for Gedaref. The EEPA report also relayed unverified claims that army chief Burhan approved sending fighters to Saudi-led operations against the Houthis, which neither Riyadh nor Yemen has confirmed.

stories.headline: S&P Puts France's A+ Rating on Negative Outlook After the CAC 40 Ends the Week 0.58% Higher at 8,156
stories.summary: S&P Global Ratings on Friday evening, 27 Nov, affirmed France at A+ but cut its outlook to negative from stable, citing weak growth, rising interest costs and political polarisation that it expects to persist beyond the 2027 presidential election. The minority government aims to trim the deficit to 5.0% of output in 2027 from 5.4% this year, while third-quarter output fell 0.1%. Earlier on 27 Nov, Insee's flash estimate showed consumer inflation slowing to 2.9% in November from 3.4%, below the 3.2% forecast, and the CAC 40 closed up 0.58% at 8,156.
stories.market: The decision landed after the close, so French government bonds (OATs) and the OAT-Bund spread get their first test on Monday 30 Nov; 10-year yields rose above 5.14% in October, the highest since 2002. On Friday, STMicro led the CAC 40 (+3.86% to €37.15) and Lumibird jumped 18.13% on a Thales takeover plan.

body: S&P kept France's sovereign rating at A+/A-1 on 27 Nov but moved the outlook to negative, meaning a downgrade is possible at a later review. It pointed to fiscal deficits that it now expects to be larger this year and next than previously forecast, as weak growth and higher interest costs make consolidation harder.

The agency said continued political polarisation, including after the 2027 presidential election, could keep limiting deficit-cutting measures and growth reforms. With the move, all three major agencies now signal downside risk to France's rating.

The minority government is trying to pass its 2027 budget through a divided parliament about five months before the presidential vote. Finance Minister Roland Lescure said the decision underlines the need for a responsible budget that brings the deficit to no more than 5%.

The macro backdrop is soft: output contracted 0.1% in the third quarter after stagnating in the second, leaving the 0.5% growth goal for 2026 nearly out of reach. Insee's flash estimate on 27 Nov put November CPI at 2.9% (HICP 3.2%), down from 3.4% (3.7%) in October, as energy inflation slowed to 19.2% from 24.1% on cheaper petroleum products.

Paris equities closed the week firmly: the CAC 40 rose 0.58% to 8,156 on 27 Nov as chip stocks rebounded, with STMicroelectronics up 3.86%. Thales said it plans to buy Lumibird, first acquiring the founder's 51.6% stake and then offering €30.10 a share including a special dividend, sending Lumibird up 18.13% to €29.

stories.headline: JPMorgan Downgrades Adidas to Neutral and Cuts Its Target 20% to €184, and Moves Puma to Underweight on 2027 Worries
stories.summary: JPMorgan cut Adidas to Neutral from Overweight on 27 Nov and lowered its price target to €184 from €230, citing a jump in discounting on Adidas.com in the US and Britain to 60-70% in November from 20-30% in August. Analyst Chiara Battistini cut her 2027 apparel growth forecast for the brand to 5%, against market consensus of 9%. The bank also downgraded Puma to Underweight from Neutral, with a target of €21, down from €26. It forecasts Puma's 2027 adjusted operating profit at €31 million, far below the €171 million consensus. Puma's third-quarter currency-adjusted sales fell 6.3%.
stories.market: Invezz reported both stocks fell on the calls on Friday (27 Nov) while the STOXX 600 rose 1.1%; JPMorgan's view is that heavier markdowns could squeeze fourth-quarter and 2027 margins across the sector.

body: JPMorgan turned more cautious on Germany's two big sportswear makers on 27 Nov. Analyst Chiara Battistini downgraded Adidas to Neutral from Overweight and cut the price target 20% to €184 from €230. Wendy Liu downgraded Puma to Underweight from Neutral and lowered the target to €21 from €26.

For Adidas, the bank's main concern is pricing. It found discounting on the company's own website in the US and Britain had risen to 60-70% in November from 20-30% in August, which it sees as a risk to fourth-quarter margins and a sign that full-price demand is softening. It now expects 2027 apparel growth of 5%, well below the 9% the market expects, and warned that markdowns could be heavier going into 2027.

Puma's turnaround is the issue for the second call. Third-quarter currency-adjusted sales fell 6.3% while costs rose, and JPMorgan said retailers are reluctant to give the brand shelf space during the overhaul. Its forecast for 2027 adjusted operating profit is €31 million, against a consensus of €171 million, with operating costs still rising.
The downgrades landed on a strong day for European equities, with the STOXX 600 up 1.1% on 27 Nov, led by chipmakers and miners.

stories.headline: Foreign Investors Extend Their Buying Streak to 19 Sessions and Rs 1.33 Lakh Crore, Yet Stay 77% Short Index Futures as the Nifty Drops 1%
stories.summary: Foreign institutional investors bought a provisional net Rs 1,634.33 crore of Indian shares on 27 Nov, a 19th straight session of buying, taking the holiday-shortened week to Rs 17,630 crore and the run since 30 Oct to Rs 1,33,178 crore. Domestic institutions sold Rs 556.42 crore on Friday after buying Rs 5,630.72 crore on Thursday. In derivatives, FIIs were 77% short in index futures as of the 26 Nov close, net short 88,469 contracts, up from 70,454 on 20 Nov. The Nifty fell 277.30 points (1.07%) to 25,607.20 on Friday and the Sensex 989.33 points to 83,339.26, ending a four-week winning run for the Nifty.
stories.market: IT led Friday's fall (Nifty IT -1.88%; TCS, Infosys and HCL Tech each down more than 2.4%), while metals rose 1.38%; the rupee weakened to about 92.98 per dollar.

body: Foreign money kept flowing into Indian cash equities through Friday, even as the market fell. Provisional exchange data showed FIIs net bought Rs 1,634.33 crore on 27 Nov after Rs 5,843.33 crore on 26 Nov, for Rs 17,630 crore across the four sessions of the holiday-shortened week. Over 19 regular sessions since 30 Oct, the total reaches Rs 1,33,178 crore.

Positioning in derivatives tells a more hedged story. As of the 26 Nov close, FIIs held 126,129 short and 37,660 long index futures contracts, 77% short and net short 88,469 contracts, deeper than the 70,454 net short a week earlier. Non-institutional clients sat on the other side at 66.1% long. Heavy cash buying paired with futures shorts is consistent with hedged exposure rather than an outright bullish bet.

stories.headline: Tata Steel's Rs 16,756 Crore Open Offer for APL Apollo Faces a 1 December Filing Deadline as Tendering Waits on Competition Approval
stories.summary: Tata Steel's open offer for up to 7,28,06,387 APL Apollo shares at Rs 2,301.40 each in cash would cost Rs 16,755.66 crore if fully taken up, according to a 28 Nov analysis of the offer documents. The detailed public statement is due on or before 1 Dec, and tendering cannot start until the Competition Commission of India approves and the US SEC grants an exemption, pushing it to roughly mid-March to April 2027, or later if the CCI opens a detailed probe. If all public holders tender, about 36.5% of shares would be accepted. APL Apollo closed at Rs 1,670 on 23 Nov, down from Rs 2,121.6 on 20 Nov, leaving the offer far above the market price. Tata Steel said on 26 Nov it is studying changes to the deal's financial structure.
stories.market: The wide gap between the Rs 2,301.40 offer and APL Apollo's price near Rs 1,670 reflects doubt over timing, acceptance and the deal's possible restructuring; Indian metal stocks rose 1.38% on 27 Nov even as the Nifty fell.

body: The mechanics of Tata Steel's open offer for APL Apollo point to a long wait for shareholders. The offer is for up to 7,28,06,387 shares at Rs 2,301.40 each in cash, with no minimum acceptance, worth Rs 16,755.66 crore at full take-up.

Tata Steel must publish the detailed public statement on or before 1 Dec. Tendering cannot open until the Competition Commission of India clears the transaction and the US SEC grants an exemption; a 28 Nov analysis estimates mid-March to April 2027, or June-August 2027 if the CCI orders a detailed investigation.

If every public shareholder tenders, the acceptance ratio would be about 36.5%, meaning most shares would be returned. That arithmetic, together with uncertainty over timing, helps explain why APL Apollo trades far below the offer: it closed at Rs 1,670 on 23 Nov after Rs 2,121.6 on 20 Nov, before the deal announcement.

Tata Steel chief executive T. V. Narendran said on 26 Nov that the companies are examining changes to the deal's financial structure after investor objections; no revised terms had been announced by 28 Nov.

stories.headline: Black Friday Online Sales Run 12.8% Ahead of Last Year, Putting Adobe's Tally on Course for a Record $13 Billion-Plus as Amazon Climbs Almost 4%
stories.summary: US shoppers spent $9.7 billion online by 6:30 p.m. ET on Black Friday (27 Nov), 12.8% more than a year earlier, according to Adobe Analytics, which now expects the day to finish between $13 billion and $13.4 billion. That beats Adobe's September forecast of $12.9 billion, which implied 9.2% growth. Adobe sees $6.1 billion on Saturday (+6%), $6.4 billion on Sunday (+7.5%) and $15.1 billion on Cyber Monday (+6.2%), making the five days from Thanksgiving to Cyber Monday worth $47.5 billion, up 7.4%. Salesforce counted $5.9 billion of US and $30.7 billion of global online sales in the first half of the day and projects $18.7 billion for the US (+4%) and $83 billion globally (+5.2%). Amazon rose 3.96% in Friday's shortened session, despite strikes at 11 German sites.
stories.market: Amazon gained 3.96% at Friday's 1 p.m. ET close while discounter Dollar Tree slipped 2.42% after a strong run earlier in the week; the S&P 500 closed 1.60% higher at 7,297.49, ending its best week since April 2025 (+5.6%).

body: The first hard read on the US holiday season came in stronger than forecasters expected. Adobe Analytics, which tracks transactions on major US retail websites, said online spending had reached $9.7 billion by 6:30 p.m. Eastern time on Friday, 27 Nov, a 12.8% rise on the same point last year. It raised its full-day estimate to $13 billion-$13.4 billion, above the $12.9 billion it had pencilled in during September.

Adobe expects the weekend to be softer in growth terms, with $6.1 billion of spending on Saturday (up 6%) and $6.4 billion on Sunday (up 7.5%), before Cyber Monday delivers $15.1 billion (up 6.2%) as the biggest online day of the season. For the five-day stretch from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday it forecasts $47.5 billion, up 7.4%, and it still expects overall holiday online growth to be similar to last year's pace.

Salesforce, which measures a different set of merchants and includes non-US shoppers, reported $5.9 billion of US and $30.7 billion of global online sales in the first half of Black Friday. Its full-day projections are $18.7 billion for the US, up 4%, and $83 billion worldwide, up 5.2%. The gap with Adobe's growth rates reflects the different samples; both point to growth, not contraction.

Retail stocks had already rallied into the holiday. Earlier in the week Kohl's jumped 14.2% and Dollar Tree 12% after raising its earnings estimate (24-25 Nov), and the National Retail Federation is forecasting holiday sales above $1 trillion. Mastercard has cautioned that part of the increase in spending reflects higher prices rather than more goods sold.

On Friday itself, Amazon rose 3.96% in the shortened session even as workers struck at 11 German sites, while Dollar Tree gave back 2.42%. The broader market finished a holiday week of strong gains: the S&P 500 closed at 7,297.49 (+1.60%), the Nasdaq-100 at 26,726.39 (+2.61%) and the Dow at 50,774.94 (+1.18%).

analysts.view: Raised its Amazon price target ahead of the holiday

detail.consensus: Early online data point to a solid start to the season, with growth above Adobe's own September forecast, though price increases flatter the dollar totals.

stories.headline: Bombay High Court Refuses Tata Trusts Any Interim Relief, Letting Monday's Tata Sons Board Meeting and the Casting Vote Stand for Now
stories.summary: Justice Abhay Ahuja of the Bombay High Court declined (27 Nov) to grant Sir Dorabji Tata Trust and RD Tata Trust any urgent relief in their challenge to N Chandrasekaran's reappointment as Tata Sons executive chairman, so the board meeting set for 30 November can go ahead. The trusts, which hold about 66% of Tata Sons, had asked for the meeting to be deferred or stayed and for the chairman to be barred from using a casting vote if their two nominee directors split. The judge said anything decided at the meeting will remain subject to the court's final orders and gave Tata Sons and the other defendants time to file replies. PTI puts the next hearing on 18 January 2027 (Business Today reports 21 January). The suits still seek to have the 17 September resolution declared void and ₹65 crore in damages.
stories.market: Tata shares had mixed moves on Friday, mostly before the 3 pm ruling: around 3:04 pm IST TCS was down 2.68% at ₹2,569.50 while Tata Steel was up 1.32% at ₹165.70 and Titan up 3.37% at ₹4,787, against a 1.18% fall in the Sensex to 83,328 (intraday figures, 27 Nov). Monday's session, on the day of the board meeting, will be the first full trading reaction; the listing question bears on Tata Sons-linked names and the Shapoorji Pallonji group's stake.

body: Friday's hearing was the first test of the suits the two largest Tata trusts filed on 26 November against Tata Sons and six of its directors. Justice Ahuja told the parties he was not granting relief at this stage and that the meeting should go on as scheduled, with its outcome subject to the final judgment. He ordered reply affidavits from Tata Sons, the other defendants and the board members.

Senior advocate Harish Salve, for Tata Sons, argued the meeting could not wait because the company must tell the Reserve Bank of India by 12 December how it will comply with the listing requirement for upper-layer non-bank lenders (Business Today cites 10 December). Abhishek Manu Singhvi, for Sir Dorabji Tata Trust, called the RBI deadline a pretext for manufactured urgency.

On the merits, the trusts say Articles 104B and 121 of Tata Sons' articles require a majority of trust-nominated directors to vote in favour of certain decisions, and that the acting chairman's casting vote on 17 September could not substitute for that. Tata Sons says the deadlock arose because the trusts appointed two nominees with opposing views, disputes that the clause works as a veto, and questions whether the suits are maintainable, including whether Charity Commissioner permission was needed.

The trusts' own board remains split. On 27 November trustees Vijay Singh and Venu Srinivasan asked the Maharashtra Charity Commissioner to look into Sir Dorabji Tata Trust's decision to litigate, adding to Singh's earlier complaint about the use of charitable funds.

According to Business Today, Monday's agenda includes confirming the minutes of the 17 September meeting, the RBI listing mandate, calling an extraordinary general meeting and fixing its date, monetising the Shapoorji Pallonji group's stake, and reviews of Tata AIG, Agratas and Tejas. Noel Tata's alternative would fold Tata Electronics Systems Solutions and Tata Consulting Engineers into Tata Sons so it stops qualifying as a core investment company that must list.

stories.headline: Irish High Court Refuses to Sanction Bawag's €1.62 Billion Takeover of Permanent TSB Over How the Shareholder Vote Was Run
stories.summary: Justice Michael Quinn of the Irish High Court declined (26 Nov) to sanction the scheme of arrangement through which Austria's Bawag Group agreed in April to buy Permanent TSB for €2.97 a share in cash, about €1.62 billion. He held that the finance minister, who owns about 57.5% of PTSB, and the other shareholders should have voted at separate meetings, so the required special majority had not been properly obtained, even though about 91% of votes cast in July backed the deal. The judge said the court was not ruling on whether the deal was good or bad, only on whether the process protected everyone's interests. PTSB said it is considering the judgment; the deal had been due to complete by the end of March 2027.
stories.market: Bawag (BG, Vienna) fell as much as 6.1% after the ruling and was down 3.4% at 16:35 Vienna time on 26 Nov. The decision puts the timetable at risk and gives activist PTSB (PTSB, Dublin) holders who wanted a higher or rival offer a stronger hand.

body: A scheme of arrangement under Irish company law needs court sanction after shareholders approve it. Quinn found that the state, as a controlling holder with interests different from other investors, formed a separate class, and that a single combined meeting therefore did not meet the statutory test.

The state is selling its last bank stake from the post-crisis bailouts. PTSB started a formal sale process after the government signalled it would sell; several boutique firms made non-binding approaches but no formal offers emerged, and Bawag's recommended cash bid followed in April 2026 with the finance minister's support.

PTSB and Bawag said they are reviewing the judgment and will update the market. Options reported include rerunning the votes with separate class meetings, though no timetable or appeal has been announced.

stories.headline: China's Supreme Court Orders Tetra Pak to Pay a Record 492 Million Yuan to Two Packaging Rivals
stories.summary: The Supreme People's Court in Beijing raised (27 Nov) the antitrust damages Tetra Pak China and related companies must pay to two domestic competitors to about 492 million yuan (roughly $74 million), the largest award in a Chinese antitrust lawsuit. Greatview's companies get 466 million yuan, up from 40.43 million yuan awarded by the Beijing High People's Court in December 2023, and Shandong Newjf gets 26.47 million yuan, up from 1.69 million yuan. The suits followed a 2016 ruling by the then State Administration for Industry and Commerce that Tetra Pak abused its dominance in liquid food packaging from 2009 to 2013, for which it was fined about 668 million yuan. The court calculated losses from the market share Tetra Pak would have lost without the conduct, using its 2015 share as the benchmark.
stories.market: Tetra Pak is privately held by Tetra Laval, so there is no direct listed read-across, but the ruling raises the cost of follow-on damages claims for dominant foreign firms in China and matters for packaging and dairy-supply groups. It is a precedent that private plaintiffs can win large sums after a regulator's finding.

body: The judgments were read in open court at the Supreme People's Court's intellectual property tribunal after all three sides appealed the 2023 first-instance awards. The court found the conduct foreclosed the market and harmed both rivals, and that its effects lasted until at least 2014, partly because Tetra Pak did not show when it stopped.

The regulator's 2016 decision identified three linked practices: stopping paper suppliers from serving rivals, tying packaging materials to equipment and technical services, and loyalty discounts. Greatview was Tetra Pak's largest Chinese competitor at the time; Newjf was a smaller, fast-growing entrant.

The court said it examined 36 new items of evidence and scrutinised the economists' reports on data and methods, and presented the case as guidance on how to prove and quantify antitrust damages. No response from Tetra Pak was reported.

stories.headline: Chile's Competition Prosecutor Asks the Antitrust Court to Fine Apple About $80 Million and Open the iPhone to Rival App Stores
stories.summary: Chile's National Economic Prosecutor's Office (FNE) filed a case (27 Nov) asking the country's antitrust court to fine Apple about $80 million, equal to 30% of sales tied to the conduct during the period investigated. It alleges Apple has abused its dominance in iOS since at least 2019 by blocking sideloading and alternative app stores, so developers and users depend on the App Store, and by restricting in-app payments, where it charges commissions of 15-30%. The FNE also wants orders requiring Apple to allow third-party stores, alternative billing and links to outside payment pages without friction. Apple says the limits protect security and privacy; the FNE found them unnecessary and disproportionate. The court will decide.
stories.market: The sum is small for Apple (AAPL), but Chile joins a list of jurisdictions pressing on App Store fees, a high-margin part of its services business. In the US, the Supreme Court hears Apple's appeal of the Epic Games contempt ruling over link-out commissions on 11 Jan 2027, with 32 states and DC filing in support of Epic last week.

body: In Chile the FNE investigates and prosecutes; fines and remedies are set by the competition tribunal. The filing seeks both the penalty and behavioural remedies that would let developers distribute apps outside the App Store, integrate rival payment systems and steer customers to outside purchase pages.
The FNE argues that restrictions on telling users about cheaper prices elsewhere blunt competitive pressure on Apple's commission. Apple's defence rests on user security and privacy.

The case lands as Apple's US contempt appeal nears argument. The district court found Apple violated an injunction by charging up to 27% on link-out purchases; the Ninth Circuit upheld the finding, and the Supreme Court will review only the legal standard used.

timeline.text: Start of the conduct alleged by the FNE (year only).

stories.headline: Korea's Fair Trade Commission Rejects White House Charge of Bias Over Its 300.8 Billion Won Coupang Fine
stories.summary: The Korea Fair Trade Commission said (27 Nov) it does not discriminate by nationality and treats US, Korean and other firms alike, answering a White House official who told Fox News on 25 Nov that Seoul was breaking a pledge to treat US tech companies, including Coupang, fairly. The KFTC fined Coupang 300.8 billion won (about $225 million) on 9 Nov for making Coupang Eats restaurants offer terms at least as good as on rival apps; that is more than seven times the 42 billion won cap it had signalled in June, after relevant sales were reassessed at 5.01 trillion won. With a 624.68 billion won privacy fine from June, Coupang's Korean penalties total about 925.5 billion won (around $688 million). A State Department official said Washington is reviewing policy options.
stories.market: The row adds regulatory and trade risk for Coupang (CPNG), which is NYSE-listed and Delaware-incorporated, and could face a further fine of more than 200 billion won in a separate tying case under re-examination. Washington has signalled possible Section 301 probes of Korean digital rules, a risk for the won and for tariff talks touching chips and cars.

body: The KFTC found that from July 2023 to January 2026 Coupang enforced most-favoured-nation terms on restaurants across six areas, including menu prices and opening hours, stripping non-compliant merchants of 'WOW Store' status that its paid members' delivery benefits depended on. Some 57,907 merchants lost the status at least once, and compliance rose from 13.49% to 93.78%. Baemin operator Woowa Brothers was fined 331.1 billion won for similar practices.

Washington points to the joint fact sheet from the November 2025 US-Korea summit, which said US firms should not face discrimination under digital rules. Rep. Darrell Issa has singled out KFTC chairman Joo Byung-ki. Korea's embassy says the decisions followed the law and that remedies remain available.

The jump in the fine came because deliberation widened the relevant sales base from about 710 billion won in the examiner's report. The KFTC has also ordered re-examination of whether Coupang illegally tied shopping and food delivery into one membership; an official gave no timeline.

stories.headline: SEBI Bars Le Lavoir's Chairman and 13 Others From Dealing in the Stock Over a Suspected Warrant-Issue Pump
stories.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India issued an interim ex-parte order (reported 26-27 Nov) barring Le Lavoir chairman Ashok Dilipkumar Jain from the securities market, stopping the BSE-listed company from raising fresh capital and restraining 13 other people and entities from trading its shares. SEBI alleges price manipulation, suspicious fund flows and irregularities in a 2025 preferential warrant issue: the company allotted 15.81 lakh warrants to 25 investors and collected about ₹10.46 crore upfront, with investors linked to Jain taking over 85% of the allotment. It says money flowed from Jain or related entities into the allottees' subscriptions and that chats with Sunshine Capital promoter Surendra Jain discussed coming announcements and expected price gains. The noticees have 21 days to respond.
stories.market: The order hits trading in Le Lavoir on the BSE and fits SEBI's continuing crackdown on small-cap preferential-issue schemes, a risk factor for India's SME and micro-cap segment. Sunshine Capital is also named in the order.

body: The order was passed by whole-time member Kamlesh Chandra Varshney. SEBI's concern is that allottees could sell once lock-ins on the preferential shares expire, leaving retail buyers exposed.

Le Lavoir first proposed warrants worth nearly ₹100 crore before scaling the issue back. Jain, his wife and daughter together received 8.78 lakh warrants. SEBI is still examining whether small-volume trades by linked traders helped lift the price.

stories.headline: Foodlink's Unofficial Premium Shrinks to ₹4 From ₹18 Ahead of Monday's Close, While Monomark and Matangi Command Double-Digit Premiums Before Next Week's Issues
stories.summary: The grey-market premium on Foodlink F&B Holdings' ₹360.76 crore IPO fell to ₹4, or about 2.1% over the ₹191 top of its price band, as of 08:02 IST on 28 Nov, from ₹18 (about 9.4%) quoted on opening day, 26 Nov. The issue was 1.42 times subscribed by day two (27 Nov), Upstox reported, and closes on 30 Nov with listing set for 3 Dec. Among next week's mainboard offers, Monomark Engineering (₹60-65, opens 2 Dec) carried a ₹20 premium (about 31%) and Matangi Rubber (₹163-172, opens 1 Dec) ₹31 (about 18%), while the largest, Swara Baby Products' ₹799.88 crore issue, showed only ₹3. The figures circulate despite SEBI's 24 Nov advisory urging registered intermediaries to stop publishing grey-market premiums, which are unregulated and carry no settlement guarantee.
stories.market: A fading premium for Foodlink after Mahanadi Coalfields' below-issue debut on 27 Nov points to cooler listing-day expectations for mid-sized issues; next week brings three mainboard offers worth more than ₹900 crore combined at the top of their bands.

body: Foodlink, a Mumbai-based premium caterer and restaurant operator with businesses in India, the UAE, the UK and Malaysia, is raising ₹192 crore in fresh shares plus a ₹168.76 crore offer for sale at ₹181-191 per share, in lots of 78 shares. It raised ₹162.34 crore from anchor investors on 25 Nov. The company earned ₹29.11 crore in FY2026 but reported a ₹16.15 crore loss for the six months to 30 Sep 2026; it is valued at about ₹1,191 crore at the top of the band.

Next week's pipeline: Matangi Rubber opens 1-3 Dec with a ₹99.10 crore fresh issue plus a ₹26.06 crore sale; Monomark Engineering opens 2-4 Dec with a fresh issue of up to 2.70 crore shares; and Swara Baby Products opens 2-4 Dec with ₹499.88 crore new shares and a ₹300 crore sale. SME issuer A J Packaging showed a ₹24 premium (about 13%) and Vishwas Refoils none.

Grey-market quotes are unofficial and have diverged from actual listing prices in several recent large IPOs, which SEBI cited when it asked intermediaries on 24 Nov to stop displaying them. Tracker sites continue to publish them with disclaimers.

stories.headline: Rial Holds Near Its Record Low of 2.965 Million per Dollar on Tehran's Open Market, Down by More Than Half in a Year
stories.summary: The US dollar sold for 2,945,000 rials (294,500 tomans) on Tehran's open market at 08:35 local time on Saturday 28 Nov, unchanged on the day after a 0.2% rise on Friday, according to tracker AlanChand, with a 24-hour range of 2.939-2.957 million. The rate sits just below the 2,965,000 high of the past week and month, and compares with about 1,127,000 at the low of the past year, meaning the dollar has more than doubled. The euro fetched 3,229,000 rials and the UAE dirham 801,800. The street rate is about 50% above the central bank's official dollar rate of 1,959,682 rials set on 26 Nov.
stories.market: The plateau below 3 million follows US sanctions on an Iranian exchange-house network on 23 Nov and a continuing US naval blockade; the dirham rate is the key channel for trade settled through the UAE and a gauge of secondary-sanctions risk for Gulf money-service businesses.

body: Buy quotes stood at 2,915,500 rials on Saturday morning, a spread of about 1% to the selling price. Over the past seven days the dollar ranged from 2,675,000 to 2,965,000 rials, showing how quickly the currency fell after the 23 Nov US Treasury action against 22 entities and 8 people in a shadow-banking network.
Rates come from an informational tracker of Tehran's open market rather than an exchange; quotes can vary between sources. The pound sterling traded at 3,824,000 rials.
The official central bank rate, used for priority imports, has drifted more slowly, leaving a gap of roughly half again between official and street dollars.

stories.headline: Naira's Street Discount Widens to ₦65 Despite the Central Bank's Cash Release, While Argentina's Blue Dollar Slips Below 1,700
stories.summary: Lagos street dealers sold dollars at ₦1,452-1,458 at Thursday's close (26 Nov), against an official NFEM close of ₦1,387.89, widening the gap to about ₦65 (4.7%) from ₦58 on Wednesday and ₦51 on Monday, WithinNigeria reported on 27 Nov. The widening came despite the central bank's move from 25 Nov to let banks sell up to $1 million a week in cash to each bureau de change. In Buenos Aires the informal blue dollar fell 5 pesos to 1,695 on Friday 27 Nov, its second straight daily drop, though it still rose 20 pesos over the week, Ámbito reported. The MEP rate closed at 1,658.32 and the CCL at 1,767.37, against a wholesale official rate of 1,605.
stories.market: A widening naira gap at year-end signals that dollar demand is outrunning the new cash supply; in Argentina, a narrow blue premium and central bank dollar purchases of $61 million on Friday point to calmer parallel markets, helped by a rebound in Brazilian assets.

body: Street dealers in Lagos were buying dollars at about ₦1,440-1,445 on Thursday. Another outlet, Punch, reported a different official close of ₦1,378, an example of how quotes vary. The central bank's reference rate was ₦1,391.75 for 25 Nov.
Gross external reserves stood at $54.251 billion on 24 Nov, down from a peak of $55.26 billion on 27 Oct. The Monetary Policy Committee held its benchmark rate at 23% at its 23-24 Nov meeting.

In Argentina the blue dollar had touched an intraday high of 1,730 on Wednesday before easing. Ámbito attributed the calmer tone to legislative progress by the government, a strong rebound in Brazilian assets after a new economy minister was named there, a Wall Street rally and talk of official intervention, while noting continued demand for currency hedging and doubts over reserve accumulation.

stories.headline: US Aircraft Disable a Chinese-Owned Bulker Leaving Bandar Abbas, the Sixth Ship Stopped Since the Iran Blockade Resumed, as Sanctioned Tankers Test the Line
stories.summary: A US military aircraft fired precision munitions at the stern of the Palau-flagged, Chinese-owned bulk carrier Pacific Archer in the Gulf of Oman on Thursday 26 Nov, disabling its propulsion after it ignored repeated warnings to stop, US Central Command said; the crew was unhurt. The 52,400-dwt ship had sailed from Iran's Bandar Abbas. CENTCOM says it is the sixth vessel disabled since the blockade resumed, the previous one on 7 Nov, while 158 vessels have complied and been redirected; reports put the total disabled since the war began in late February at least 15. Tracking firm Windward reported that the sanctioned product tanker Voyager Haven headed for Djibouti under a false Malian registry, while another sanctioned tanker, World Progress, stopped short of the US line.
stories.market: Kinetic enforcement against non-tanker cargo widens the risk for owners and insurers trading with Iranian ports, keeping a sanctions premium in Gulf freight and war-risk insurance and squeezing Iran's hard-currency earnings.

body: Pacific Archer is a 2001-built bulk carrier. Its cargo was not disclosed. The strike marks a shift in tempo after nearly three weeks without a disabled vessel.

Windward's tracking shows sanctioned ships using false registries to try to slip the cordon: Voyager Haven claims Malian registry, and World Progress falsely claims Cook Islands registry while broadcasting under another name and the Marshall Islands flag.
Iranian officials have largely dismissed reports of a planned convoy to challenge the blockade. President Trump is reported to be weighing next steps.

stories.headline: Trump Backs Baghdad's Oil-Smuggling Crackdown as Iraq Shuts Two Kurdish-Region Crossings to Iran and Syria
stories.summary: President Trump said on 27 Nov that Washington supports Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi's drive to stop oil smuggling, end corruption and bring all weapons under state control, Al Jazeera reported. A day earlier Iraq's border forces closed the Bashta crossing with Iran and the Al Waleed crossing with Syria, both in territory run by the Kurdistan Regional Government. Government spokesman Haider al-Aboudi said Baghdad estimates about $100 billion was lost to smuggling through the Kurdish region between 2008 and 2025, a figure whose basis Reuters said was unclear. The KRG denies illicit oil operations and says it rejects violations of its constitutional rights, while thousands protested in Erbil on 26 Nov.
stories.market: US backing strengthens Baghdad's hand in curbing leakage of Iraqi crude into grey channels serving sanctioned Iran, but the standoff raises disruption risk for northern exports and Kurdistan-focused producers ahead of 1 Dec talks.

body: Oil Minister Basim Mohammed said Iraq would show no leniency toward oil exported outside legal channels. Al-Zaidi has also ordered the army to prepare to enter Jurf al-Sakhar, south of Baghdad, where the government accuses the Iran-backed Kataib Hezbollah of running a smuggling operation.

KRG spokesman Peshawa Hawramani said the region does not want clashes. The KRG says it is working with federal authorities against corruption and on 25 Nov rejected what it called military language and threats from the Iraqi military spokesman. Baghdad denies that army units are moving north.

Iraqi government figures cited earlier this week put current smuggling at 200,000-230,000 barrels a day, worth about $200 million a month. A meeting sponsored by the head of the Supreme Judicial Council is scheduled in Baghdad on 1 Dec.

stories.headline: Paraguay's Former Economy Minister Surrenders on Laundering and Bribery Charges Over Ueno Bank, Joining a Jailed Ex-President and Central Bank Chiefs
stories.summary: Carlos Fernández Valdovinos, Paraguay's economy minister until March 2026, turned himself in to organised-crime police in Asunción shortly before 1 p.m. on Friday 27 Nov, after a warrant accusing him of administration for personal gain, aggravated passive bribery, criminal association and money laundering. Prosecutors say that in July 2025 he authorised the investment of 250 billion guaraníes (about $38.8 million) of a state pension fund in Ueno Bank certificates of deposit, then signed a consulting contract with the bank's controlling Grupo Vázquez after leaving office. Ueno, the country's largest digital bank with nearly 3 million customers and about 9% of system deposits, was placed in resolution on 3 Nov, locking customers out of their accounts. Former president Santiago Peña, removed by the Senate on 6 Nov, remains in pretrial detention alongside a former central bank president and a former bank superintendent.
stories.market: The case widens the fallout from the failure of a bank holding roughly a tenth of Paraguay's deposits, with uninsured depositors and the state pension institute IPS still awaiting recovery; it is a test of deposit-guarantee capacity and governance in a small dollar-bond issuer.

body: Fernández Valdovinos, 61, presented himself at the Dirección Contra el Crimen Organizado on Friday and was held ahead of formal questioning set for Saturday 28 Nov at 10:30 a.m. at the prosecutors' economic crimes and anti-corruption unit. Six prosecutors are working the file, according to Noticias Argentinas.

The accusation centres on a ministerial resolution of 28 July 2025 authorising the state pensions directorate to place 250 billion guaraníes of the Caja Fiscal in Ueno certificates of deposit. Prosecutors allege the minister accepted a promise of personal compensation from banker Federico Vázquez Villasanti in return, and point to a strategic consulting contract later signed with Grupo Vázquez. The value of that contract has not been disclosed.

Ueno's collapse began on 3 Nov, when the central bank opened resolution proceedings after the bank's solvency ratio fell below half the legal minimum; central bank chief Carlos Carvallo resigned the same day. By 11 Nov guarantee advances had been paid to 1,812,348 eligible depositors, in full or up to the insured limit, but large deposits and investments above the guarantee remained unresolved in mid-November.

Investigators are examining about $146 million of loans to three companies linked to Grupo Vázquez. The state social security institute IPS reportedly had about $358 million of pension reserves at Ueno and roughly $515 million of total exposure including operating funds.

The political toll is unprecedented: the Senate voted 44-0 to remove President Peña on 6 Nov and he was arrested that evening; he denies wrongdoing. His brother is in preventive detention, and four former central bank officials have been charged and jailed.

stories.headline: North Korea-Linked Launderers Push More Than $600 Million of Binance Loot Through THORChain as $1.13 Billion in Stolen Bitcoin Sits Untouched
stories.summary: Launderers tied to the 29 Oct Binance theft have swapped about 125,000 ether (roughly $210 million) into about 3,470 bitcoin since 17 Nov, mostly via the cross-chain protocol THORChain, Elliptic said in tracker data updated on 26 Nov. Chainalysis and Elliptic estimate more than $600 million has passed through THORChain overall, though Elliptic warns of possible double-counting, and at least 6,330 BTC (about $389 million) has been through a bitcoin coinjoin coordinator. THORChain co-founder Chad Barraford said on 26 Nov the protocol cannot block addresses and that 98% of its volume is legitimate, despite an FBI request on 31 Oct. About $2.85 billion of the haul is frozen, while the 18,270 BTC (about $1.13 billion) taken directly from Binance has not moved.
stories.market: Laundering flows keep regulatory pressure on decentralised swap venues and their RUNE token, while the large unmoved bitcoin stash is a potential supply overhang that analysts watch for exchange deposits; none had been reported as of 27 Nov.

body: A day after Binance said its withdrawal freeze was fully lifted, blockchain researchers published the clearest picture yet of how the proceeds are being moved. Elliptic attributes the activity to North Korea's TraderTraitor group, as the FBI does; Pyongyang denies involvement.

The ether-to-bitcoin swaps paused from 21 to 23 Nov, then resumed at more than 20,000 ETH a day before slowing sharply around 09:30 UTC on 26 Nov. Elliptic says the activity spans tens of thousands of wallets, 16 blockchains and about 55 services, and that about $16 million went to addresses also holding proceeds of September's Bitget exploit.

THORChain has declined to censor transactions. TRM Labs estimates the protocol may have earned up to about $1 million in fees from the flows, and its Ari Redbord said full laundering could take months or years.

Large balances remain dormant: about 347,000 ETH (about $602 million) in untouched batches, about 41,000 ETH in four large addresses, and the 18,270 BTC taken directly from Binance. The US Justice Department filed on 23 Nov to forfeit more than $1.1 billion in frozen USDC.

stories.headline: Macau and Zhuhai Police Arrest 20 in a Gold-for-Crypto Laundering Ring Serving Southeast Asian Scam Gangs, as US Tallies $1.08 Billion Restrained
stories.summary: Police in Macau and neighbouring Zhuhai have jointly broken up a gang accused of laundering more than 13 million patacas (about 10.84 million yuan) for overseas fraud operations by buying gold obtained through Southeast Asian telecom-fraud syndicates and reselling it through mainland jewellery stores, with transactions settled in cryptocurrency, Caixin reported on 27 Nov. Twenty people were arrested and three alleged ringleaders were remanded on fraud, laundering and criminal-association charges; the activity spanned June 2025 to January 2026 and at least 36 fraud cases. The bust comes as the US Justice Department's anti-scam drive reports more than 800 defendants in over 400 cases, with its Scam Center Strike Force having traced and restrained $1.08 billion in crypto.
stories.market: Gold-and-crypto conversion channels draw scrutiny to jewellery retailers, OTC desks and stablecoin rails in the Greater Bay Area; tighter enforcement raises compliance costs for exchanges serving the region.

body: Police seized cash, phones, computers and crypto wallets worth about 130,000 patacas, along with gold-trading records. The three alleged masterminds are in custody pending trial.

In the US, the Justice Department says its campaign under Executive Order 14390, signed on 6 March, has reached 85 federal districts. Separately, the FBI's Operation Blackout reports nearly $17 billion of illicit funds restrained, mostly bitcoin tied to the Prince Group case, more than 14,000 devices seized and 29 scam compounds dismantled, Blockhead reported.

About 127,271 bitcoin is the subject of a US civil forfeiture action against Prince Group, whose chairman Chen Zhi has been indicted; Treasury has sanctioned 226 Prince-linked targets. On 19 Nov Treasury also sanctioned a Cambodian scam operator and two commanders of the Democratic Karen Benevolent Army.

stories.headline: Bank of England Says Private-Credit Stress Has Risen and Flags Zero-Haircut Repo Lending to Hedge Funds, While Cutting Bank Capital Requirements
stories.summary: The Bank of England's Financial Policy Committee said in its Financial Stability Report on 26 Nov that credit stress has increased in parts of private credit since July, though less so among UK borrowers, citing a Fitch estimate that the US private-credit default rate reached 6.3% in the 12 months to September, up from 5.4% a year earlier. It warned that private markets, at about $2.5 trillion, have not been tested by a broad macroeconomic stress at their current size, and that 39% of private-credit debt matures by end-2029. On shadow banking, it said hedge-fund leverage remains elevated and that Bank analysis found a sizeable volume of zero-haircut gilt repo lending to hedge funds. At the same time it completed a capital review that will cut major UK banks' Tier 1 requirements by about 50 basis points of risk-weighted assets.
stories.market: The warning adds an official voice to concern over private-credit marks and refinancing, relevant to BDCs and listed managers such as Blackstone, Apollo, Ares and Blue Owl, while lower capital requirements are a support for UK bank stocks; planned gilt repo reforms target hedge-fund basis trades.

body: The FPC said overall vulnerabilities were not materially changed but singled out private credit's floating-rate structure, which leaves borrowers exposed to higher interest costs, and a growing share of UK corporate private-credit debt maturing within three years. Global private-credit assets under management grew 17% in the 12 months to end-2025.

The Bank also linked private credit to the AI investment boom, citing Morgan Stanley's estimate of $700 billion of 2026-2028 data-centre capex financed by private credit and J.P. Morgan's estimate that $1.4 trillion of AI capex could be funded by alternative capital. Internal estimates put hyperscalers' total potential exposure, including off-balance-sheet commitments, at just over $4 trillion, and the Bank noted sharply wider spreads for some lower-quality AI-related borrowers.

On non-bank leverage, the report said hedge-fund deleveraging contributed to the rise in French sovereign yields with limited spillover to gilts, and that central clearing of gilt repo could unlock up to £19 billion of extra intermediation capacity in normal conditions and £24 billion in stress. A roadmap is due in the first half of 2027.
The Bank's system-wide exploratory scenario on private markets will give an initial update in early 2027 and a full report in the second quarter of 2027. The countercyclical buffer stays at 2%.

stories.headline: Japan Tobacco Closes 4.5% Higher on Imperial Talk as Altria Recovers From an Early Drop; Analysts Flag Leverage and a Dividend Squeeze
stories.summary: Japan Tobacco shares closed up 4.5% in Tokyo on 27 Nov, against a 1.7% rise in the TOPIX, after Bloomberg reported it was weighing a joint all-cash approach for Imperial Brands with Altria. Altria fell more than 2.5% early in Friday's US half-day session but recovered to close 0.80% higher. Imperial's 13.3% jump on 26 Nov had lifted its market value to about £25.9 billion ($34 billion); neither suitor has yet named a price. Morningstar warned a deal could push Altria's net leverage to its highest ever, while Altria's own balance sheet shows $2.7 billion of cash against about $24 billion of debt and a dividend costing about $7.4 billion a year. Altria has until 5 p.m. London time on 24 Dec to make a firm offer or walk away.
stories.market: Japan Tobacco (2914.T) outpaced the TOPIX by almost three points on 27 Nov; Altria (MO) ended Friday 0.80% higher near $76 after early losses, and Imperial (IMB.L) holds most of Thursday's 13.3% gain.

body: The market spent Friday pricing who might pay for Imperial Brands and how. Japan Tobacco closed 4.5% higher in Tokyo on 27 Nov, outperforming a 1.7% gain in the TOPIX, after Bloomberg reported that it and Altria were considering a joint all-cash offer. Japan Tobacco declined to comment. Altria said on 26 Nov that it is weighing a possible, likely all-cash bid and is talking to an unnamed party about buying part of Imperial's business.

In New York, Altria slid more than 2.5% early in the shortened Black Friday session as investors weighed the funding burden, then recovered to finish 0.80% higher. A Finexus analysis put Altria's cash at $2.7 billion against roughly $24 billion of debt and $9.1 billion of trailing free cash flow, with net debt at 1.9 times EBITDA; its dividend of $4.44 a share on about 1.66 billion shares costs about $7.4 billion a year, a payout ratio near 92%.

Analysts quoted by Reuters sketched a carve-up in which Japan Tobacco takes Imperial's US business, possibly with other regions, while Altria takes some or all of the international assets. Imperial's African and Middle Eastern operations would fit Japan Tobacco's expansion in Africa and could help replace revenue it lost when Russia seized its Russian subsidiaries earlier this month, a move for which JT has said it will book an $8.7 billion loss.

Morningstar's Kristoffer Inton warned that a deal could push Altria to its highest net leverage ever and take several years to bring back to target even if share buybacks were paused. BTIG's Owen Bennett said a deal could be structured without hurting either buyer's credit rating, partly by reissuing about $7.4 billion of Japan Tobacco's treasury shares; JT held ¥887.3 billion ($5.6 billion) of cash at end-September. Jefferies' Andrei Andon-Ionita said Imperial holders would likely welcome offers above the company's five-year peak price-earnings multiple of 9.6 times.

Imperial, whose shares closed 13.3% higher at 3,432p on 26 Nov, has said it has received no approach. Its Friday close could not be confirmed from sources read for this edition. Under the UK Takeover Code, Altria must announce a firm intention to bid or walk away by 5 p.m. London time on 24 Dec unless the Takeover Panel grants an extension.

Imperial holders likely to welcome offers above the 9.6x five-year peak P/E; deal could make JT a sizeable third-place US player

detail.consensus: Analysts see a regional split between Japan Tobacco and Altria as the likeliest structure, with Altria's leverage and dividend the main constraint.

stories.headline: Leveraged Chip ETF Leads $3.5 Billion of Inflows as Gold and Bitcoin Funds Bleed, While Goldman Sees Hedge Funds Piling Into ETF Shorts
stories.summary: The Direxion Daily Semiconductor Bull 3x ETF (SOXL) took in $3.5 billion in the week to 25 Nov, the most of any US ETF, per ETFiQ data, followed by QQQ at $3.1 billion and the short-Treasury SGOV at $2.4 billion. The gold fund GLD and BlackRock's bitcoin fund IBIT each lost $1.9 billion, and US spot bitcoin ETFs are heading for record November outflows of $5.39 billion. Goldman Sachs' Vincent Lin said on 26 Nov that hedge funds' ETF short positions jumped about 19 percentage points in the prior week, the third-largest weekly rise in a decade, after five weeks of cutting equity exposure. Funds rotated out of technology into consumer staples, utilities and REITs and added shorts in homebuilders.
stories.market: SOXL surged 14.21% on 27 Nov as chip stocks rebounded, a setup in which heavy ETF shorts could fuel further short-covering; IBIT fell 0.62% and GLD rose 2.12% on Friday despite the outflows.

body: ETF flow data for the week to 25 Nov show retail and tactical money buying the chip rebound with leverage. SOXL, a triple-leveraged semiconductor fund, led all US ETFs with $3.5 billion of inflows, according to ETFiQ, ahead of the Nasdaq-100 tracker QQQ at $3.1 billion. Cash-like short Treasury fund SGOV added $2.4 billion.

On the other side, TCAF had the biggest outflow at $3.1 billion, and the SPDR Gold Shares fund and BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust each lost $1.9 billion. US spot bitcoin ETFs are on course for record November outflows of $5.39 billion.

Professional investors were moving the other way. Goldman Sachs' Vincent Lin said on 26 Nov that hedge funds had cut equity exposure for five straight weeks before switching to adding shorts, with ETF short positions rising by about 19 percentage points in the prior week, the third-largest weekly increase Goldman has recorded in a decade. Gross and net exposure is at multi-year lows, according to a separate report on Goldman's data.

Funds moved out of technology into consumer staples, utilities and REITs and increased bets against cyclical consumer names such as homebuilders. Average hedge fund returns have fallen from the mid-to-high teens at mid-year to about 7%, by the same account. Lin favours hyperscale data-centre operators and sees healthcare as better value than staples.
Friday's moves showed the risk in crowded hedges: SOXL jumped 14.21% on 27 Nov and QQQ 2.69%, as the S&P 500 capped its best week since April 2025.

stories.headline: Lula Names Bradesco Chairman Trabuco as Finance Minister; the Real Extends Its Rally as the Ibovespa Locks In a 6.1% Week
stories.summary: President Lula confirmed after Thursday's close that Bradesco board chairman Luiz Carlos Trabuco Cappi will run the finance ministry from January 2027, a choice investors read as a signal of fiscal discipline. On 27 Nov the commercial dollar fell to about R$5.56 (Rio Times), more than 3% below Thursday's R$5.744 and a fifth straight decline, while the Ibovespa slipped 0.13% to 176,573.35 but ended the week 6.13% higher, its best week since the first election round.

body: The speculation that drove Thursday's 6.07% surge became fact within hours: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva announced after the 26 Nov close that Luiz Carlos Trabuco Cappi, the 75-year-old chairman of Bradesco's board, will be his finance minister when the next term begins in January 2027. Investors have treated the pick of a veteran private-sector banker as a sign that the government intends to hold the line on spending.

The currency carried most of Friday's reaction. The commercial dollar extended its slide for a fifth session, closing near R$5.56 according to The Rio Times (Suno reported a lower R$5.515), against R$5.744 on Thursday; the central bank's PTAX midday reference rate was 5.5430. The Rio Times put the dollar 6.6% below its 20 Nov high of 5.95.

Equities paused after the jump. Domestic, rate-sensitive names extended gains as futures rates eased.

Even after the rally the index remains about 15.5% below its 9 Oct peak of 209,067, by The Rio Times' count. With the Selic at 13.75%, prediction-market pricing cited by the paper puts a December hold at about 92%.

stories.headline: Turkey's Central Bank Halts One-Week Repo Auctions, a Back-Door Tightening of About 3 Points; Borsa Istanbul Gains 2.2%
stories.summary: The central bank temporarily suspended its one-week repo auctions on 27 Nov, pushing banks onto overnight funding at 39%, which former CBRT chief economist Hakan Kara estimates raises funding costs by about 3 points, and lifted remuneration on lira reserve requirements to 90% of its average funding cost from 86%. Koç University's Selva Demiralp said the step makes a December rate cut very unlikely; the BIST 100 still rose 2.18% to 10,977.01, though banks fell 1.02%.
stories.market: Economists read the move as a defence of the lira, which traded near 50.78 per dollar on 27 Nov (Aposto); industrials (+2.72%) and holdings (+1.32%) led the index while VakıfBank fell about 5% in the morning.

body: The Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey took two liquidity steps on 27 Nov without touching its headline policy rate. It paused its one-week repo tenders, its main funding channel, and raised the interest it pays on lira reserve requirements to 90% of its weighted average funding cost from 86%, saying the latter supports macro-financial stability and monetary transmission.

Economists described the package as tightening by other means. Hakan Kara of Bilkent University said banks are now funded at the 39% overnight rate, about 3 points dearer, and that the reserve-requirement change partly cushions banks' capital. Selva Demiralp of Koç University, who had expected a 100bp December cut, said a cut is now very unlikely, citing reserve-loss risks from weaker global risk appetite, lower gold prices and dollarisation after a fund-sector crisis. Atilla Yeşilada called it back-door monetary tightening.

Equities shrugged off the move outside the banks. The BIST 100 rose 233.9 points to 10,977.01 and the BIST 30 gained 2.31%, while the banking index fell 1.02% after recovering from intraday lows. On the same day, officials said about 199.25 billion lira of payments would reach 122 of 131 funds being liquidated, and Yusuf Kenan Bağır was appointed head of banking regulator BDDK.
Third-quarter GDP has not yet been published; economists surveyed by local media put annual growth at about 2.7%.

stories.headline: Kyiv Drops VAT and Excise Increases From Its Revised 2027 Budget, Leaving a €70 Billion Gap, With a Vote Set for 9 Dec
stories.summary: Ukraine's Cabinet approved a revised 2027 budget draft for its second reading on 27 Nov, removing planned VAT and excise increases worth about UAH67 billion and nearly UAH65 billion of expected customs revenue, while raising the forecast transfer from National Bank profits by UAH36.3 billion to at least UAH85 billion. Security and defence get almost UAH5 trillion, or 43% of GDP, and war-risk insurance funding rises to UAH31 billion from UAH1 billion. A financing gap of about €70 billion remains even if pledged aid arrives, and the Rada is scheduled to vote on 9 Dec.
